approved: Better and Fairer Schools (Funding and Reform) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a path for all schools to receive full and fair funding.
It would change how the Commonwealth's share of school funding is set, moving from fixed rules in the Act to regulations that can be adjusted for each jurisdiction.
The Commonwealth's share for government schools could not fall below 20 percent, or below 40 percent for the Northern Territory from 2029.
Removes transitional provisions that set the Commonwealth share of school funding.
Lets the Commonwealth share be set by regulation, with a minimum percentage for government schools.
Allows different Commonwealth shares for different states and territories.
Requires the minister to consult the Ministerial Council before setting the share.
Exempts those regulations from being disallowed by Parliament.
Adds transparency and accountability as a purpose of the Act and requires an annual ministerial statement to Parliament.
All Australian schools, particularly government schools, and the states and territories that fund them.

This means that the wording of the usual motion will remain unchanged. The amendment had been moved by Ryan MP [Elizabeth Watson-Brown](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/ryan/elizabeth_watson-brown) (Greens). ### Amendment text > *That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *“whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House is of the opinion that the Government should raise the Commonwealth contribution to public schools to at least 25% of the schooling resource standard, so as to ensure that all public schools in Australia are fully funded in 2025”.*
